# Matrix calculus identities {#sec-identities}

These identities support @sec-matrix-calculus. Throughout, $\vect{x}$ is a vector of variables, $\vect{a}$ and $\vect{b}$ are constant vectors, and $\M{A}$ is a constant matrix.

## A note on layout

The gradient of a scalar $f(\vect{x})$ can be written as a column (the same shape as $\vect{x}$) or as a row. This book uses **columns**, sometimes called *denominator layout*. With this choice, the gradient $\nabla f$ points in the direction of steepest increase, and the Jacobian of a vector function $\vect{f}(\vect{x})$ has one **row** per component of $\vect{f}$:

$$
\M{J} = \mat{\dfrac{\partial f_1}{\partial x_1} & \cdots & \dfrac{\partial f_1}{\partial x_n} \\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ \dfrac{\partial f_m}{\partial x_1} & \cdots & \dfrac{\partial f_m}{\partial x_n}}.
$$

Some books, especially in statistics and machine learning, use the other layout. Their results are the transposes of the ones here.

## Gradients of scalar functions of a vector

| $f(\vect{x})$ | $\nabla f(\vect{x})$ | Notes |
|:--|:--|:--|
| $\vect{a}\T\vect{x}$ or $\vect{x}\T\vect{a}$ | $\vect{a}$ | |
| $\vect{x}\T\vect{x} = \lVert\vect{x}\rVert^2$ | $2\vect{x}$ | |
| $\vect{x}\T\M{A}\vect{x}$ | $(\M{A} + \M{A}\T)\vect{x}$ | $2\M{A}\vect{x}$ when $\M{A}$ is symmetric |
| $\lVert\M{A}\vect{x} - \vect{b}\rVert^2$ | $2\M{A}\T(\M{A}\vect{x} - \vect{b})$ | Setting this to zero gives the normal equations |
| $\lVert\vect{x}\rVert$ | $\vect{x} / \lVert\vect{x}\rVert$ | For $\vect{x} \neq \zerovec$ |

## Jacobians of vector functions

| $\vect{f}(\vect{x})$ | Jacobian $\M{J}$ |
|:--|:--|
| $\M{A}\vect{x}$ | $\M{A}$ |
| $\vect{x}$ | $\M{I}$ |
| $\vect{g}(\vect{h}(\vect{x}))$ | $\M{J}_{\vect{g}}\big(\vect{h}(\vect{x})\big)\,\M{J}_{\vect{h}}(\vect{x})$ (chain rule) |

## Hessians

| $f(\vect{x})$ | Hessian $\nabla^2 f$ |
|:--|:--|
| $\vect{a}\T\vect{x}$ | $\M{0}$ |
| $\vect{x}\T\M{A}\vect{x}$ | $\M{A} + \M{A}\T$ |
| $\lVert\M{A}\vect{x} - \vect{b}\rVert^2$ | $2\M{A}\T\M{A}$ |

## Derivatives with respect to a matrix

For a scalar function of a matrix $\M{X}$, the derivative $\partial f / \partial \M{X}$ is the matrix with entries $\partial f / \partial x_{ij}$.

| $f(\M{X})$ | $\partial f / \partial \M{X}$ |
|:--|:--|
| $\operatorname{tr}(\M{A}\M{X})$ | $\M{A}\T$ |
| $\operatorname{tr}(\M{X}\T\M{A})$ | $\M{A}$ |
| $\operatorname{tr}(\M{X}\T\M{A}\M{X})$ | $(\M{A} + \M{A}\T)\M{X}$ |
| $\det \M{X}$ | $\det(\M{X})\,(\M{X}^{-1})\T$ |
| $\ln \lvert\det \M{X}\rvert$ | $(\M{X}^{-1})\T$ |

The standard reference for many more identities is *The Matrix Cookbook* [@petersen2012matrix].
